sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: To express possession, Hungarian commonly uses a possessed noun with a dative possessor and van/vannak.

When a vowel-final noun like autó takes a 3rd-person-plural possessive suffix, Hungarian inserts a linking -j-: autó + juk → autójuk ('their car'). That linking j shows up across many suffixes whenever a vowel would otherwise bump straight into another vowel.
